chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Gatherings of the people of religion are a nobility of this world and the Hereafter.'

key_terms.أَهْل الدِّين: The people of religion — those committed to religious observance and knowledge, scholars and the devout
key_terms.شَرَف: Nobility, honor, eminence — a quality that elevates one's standing in society and before God
key_terms.مُجَالَسَة: Sitting together, companionship, gatherings — implies ongoing social association, not just a single meeting

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the gatherings of religious people in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) that declares sitting with religious people — those devoted to faith — to be an honor that elevates one's status in both this life and the next. This hadith encouraged early Muslims in Kufa and Medina, who faced social pressure to associate with worldly elites, to instead prioritize the company of scholars and the pious.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The gatherings of the people of the Religion is a nobility in the world and the Hereafter’’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ‘Ism’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadha from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Hazim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“The holy Prophet said, ‘Association with religious people is a honor in this life as well as in the next life.’”
